ADDRESSED_RESPONSES

RESPONSE_TO Gemini | Your scoped-gamma point is directionally right, but “unique target-code findings” is still incomplete unless closure state is represented separately from discovery state.
Evidence: Duane gamma uses cumulative discoveries; if we collapse to unique-only without tracking open/closed, a review that finds 10 unique issues and closes 9 looks identical to one that finds 10 and closes 0. Exp 31’s failure mode was exactly inability to act on agreement despite kappa=0.619.

RESPONSE_TO CC2 | On your question: do not subtract closures from cumulative Duane counts. That changes the underlying model into a non-monotone process and makes gamma incomparable across experiments.
Evidence: cumulative discovery in Duane is monotone by construction. The correct adaptation is two metrics: gamma on cumulative unique target-code discoveries, plus a separate open-findings contraction metric. Exp 31 shows discovery slowdown after R7, but no closure signal; that is why gamma lagged the HIL’s qualitative convergence claim.

VERDICTS
CONFIRM CC2_F001
EXTEND CC2_F001 | Primary efficiency metric should be unique_open_findings/Kchar or unique_verified_findings/Kchar depending phase; novel-only still overcounts already-closed discoveries.
CONFIRM CC2_F004
CHALLENGE Gemini_F002 | Adding CLOSED as a bare verdict is unsafe and under-specified.
Evidence: Exp 31 already had substantial agreement with zero contraction. A new token does not fix closure unless tied to canonical ID, closure reason, and independent evidence; otherwise it recreates deferential false closure under a different name.
CONFIRM Gemini_F003
CONFIRM Gemini_F005
CONFIRM Codex_R3_F002
EXTEND Codex_R3_F005 | Stop rule should be state-based first, gamma advisory second; otherwise cumulative gamma will again under-report convergence after closure machinery starts working.

ROUND_SUMMARY

The main correction is architectural, not cosmetic: do not try to force cumulative Duane gamma to do the job of an open-state convergence metric. For the next experiment, shorten to 8 rounds, replace full-broadcast with a registry-centric star topology, reduce to 3 primary reviewers plus 1 escalation reviewer, and use CC2 sub-agents only as a replacement for external reviewer count. The stop rule should be conjunctive and state-based: open canonical target-code findings drive termination; gamma remains advisory.
